ai.literal: The letter A having as first letters all; primordial God having as first indeed the world.
ai.translation: All letters have the letter A as their beginning. The world has the primordial God as its beginning.
ai.modern: எழுத்துக்கள் எல்லாம் அகரத்தை அடிப்படையாகக் கொண்டுள்ளன. அதுபோல, இந்த உலகம் ஆதி பகவனை அடிப்படையாகக் கொண்டுள்ளது.
ai.explanation: This couplet establishes the foundational nature of the divine by comparing it to language. Just as the vowel 'A' (அகரம்) is the first sound and the basis for all other letters in the Tamil alphabet, the primordial God (ஆதி பகவன்) is the origin and sustaining principle of the entire world. The word 'முதல்' (first or beginning) is used twice to emphasize this structural parallel between the alphabet and the universe.

ai.literal: By having learned, the use that has become is what indeed, pure knower's good feet they do not worship if?
ai.translation: What is the use of all that one has learned, if they do not worship the good feet of the one with pure knowledge?
ai.modern: தூய அறிவினை உடையவனின் நல்ல திருவடிகளை வணங்கவில்லை என்றால், ஒருவர் கற்ற கல்வியினால் ஆகிய பயன் என்ன?
ai.explanation: This couplet questions the ultimate purpose of acquiring knowledge. It states that all learning is useless if it does not lead one to revere the source of pure, unblemished knowledge. The word 'வால்' means pure or white, describing an intelligence that is flawless. True education must culminate in humility and devotion to this highest wisdom.

ai.literal: Flower-upon he-who-went glorious feet they-who-reached earth-upon long they-will-live.
ai.translation: Those who reach the glorious feet of the one who walked upon the flower will live long upon the earth.
ai.modern: மலரின் மீது நடந்தவனின் மாண்புமிக்க திருவடிகளைச் சேர்ந்தவர்கள், இந்த உலகின் மீது நெடுங்காலம் வாழ்வார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet states that those who reach the glorious feet of the divine will live a long and enduring life on earth. The phrase 'மலர்மிசை ஏகினான்' literally means 'he who went upon the flower', presenting a vivid and gentle image of the divine. By uniting with ('சேர்ந்தார்') these excellent feet ('மாண் அடி'), a person secures a lasting and prosperous life ('நீடு வாழ்வார்') in this world.

ai.literal: Desiring not-desiring he-who-is-without foot to-those-who-joined anywhere suffering they-are-not.
ai.translation: For those who have reached the feet of the one who has neither desire nor aversion, there is never any suffering.
ai.modern: விருப்பு வெறுப்பு இல்லாதவனுடைய அடிகளைச் சேர்ந்தவர்களுக்கு எக்காலத்திலும் எவ்விடத்திலும் துன்பங்கள் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the benefit of attaching oneself to the one who is free from worldly attachments. The phrase 'வேண்டுதல் வேண்டாமை இலான்' refers to one who is completely free from both desire and aversion. 'அடி சேர்ந்தார்க்கு' means those who have reached or taken refuge in his feet. 'யாண்டும்' means at any time or in any place, emphasizing absolute protection. Therefore, those who align themselves with this state of desirelessness will never experience 'இடும்பை' or suffering.

ai.literal: Darkness-joining two-actions-both will-not-join God's reality-joining glory those-who-desired with.
ai.translation: The two kinds of actions born of darkness will not touch those who love the true glory of God.
ai.modern: இறைவனின் உண்மையான புகழை விரும்பிப் போற்றுபவர்களிடம், அறியாமை என்னும் இருளால் வரும் நல்வினை, தீவினை ஆகிய இரண்டு வினைகளும் சேராது.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how devotion frees a person from the cycle of karma. The phrase iruḷ cēr iruviṉai refers to the two types of actions, good and bad, that stem from the darkness of delusion or ignorance. These actions bind the soul to the cycle of birth and death. However, these actions will not attach themselves to those who love and meditate upon the true, meaningful glory of God. By focusing on the ultimate reality, the devotee transcends the ignorance that causes worldly karma.

ai.translation: Those who stand on the true path of conduct of the One who extinguished the desires of the five senses will live long.

ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of following the virtuous path set by the Divine. The phrase poṟivāyil aintu avittāṉ refers to the One who has completely subdued the desires flowing through the five channels of the sense organs. Poy tīr oḻukka neṟi describes a path of conduct that is entirely free from falsehood. By steadfastly standing on this true path, individuals achieve a lasting, eternal life.

ai.literal: To himself comparison he who does not have, feet to those who joined except, mental worry removing is difficult.
ai.translation: Except for those who have reached the feet of the one who has no equal, it is difficult to dispel the sorrows of the mind.
ai.modern: தனக்கு நிகர் இல்லாதவனுடைய திருவடிகளைச் சேர்ந்தவர்களுக்கு அல்லாமல், மற்றவர்களுக்கு மனக்கவலையை மாற்றுவது கடினம்.
ai.explanation: This couplet states that true relief from mental anguish comes only from seeking the one who is incomparable. The word 'உவமை' means comparison or equal, highlighting the supreme nature of this entity. 'தாள் சேர்ந்தார்க்கு' refers to those who have surrendered to or reached his feet. Without this connection, the text asserts that removing the mind's inherent worries ('மனக்கவலை') is exceedingly difficult.

ai.literal: Virtue ocean gracious-one feet to-those-who-reached except, other oceans swimming difficult.
ai.translation: Except for those who have reached the feet of the gracious one who is an ocean of virtue, it is difficult to cross the other oceans.
ai.modern: அறக்கடலாக விளங்கும் அந்தணனின் திருவடிகளைச் சேர்ந்தவர்களுக்கு அல்லாமல், மற்றவர்களுக்குப் பிற கடல்களை நீந்திக் கடப்பது கடினம்.
ai.explanation: The couplet describes the divine as an ocean of virtue and a gracious being. The word ஆழி can mean a wheel or an ocean, but ocean best fits the context of swimming (நீந்தல்) mentioned later in the couplet. It states that only those who reach the feet of this gracious one can cross the ocean of life. For anyone else, swimming across the other oceans of worldly existence is exceedingly difficult.

words.gloss: of the one with eight qualities

ai.literal: Perception without sense-organ-like quality they-are-without-indeed, eight-qualities-having-one's feet not-bowing head.
ai.translation: A head that does not bow to the feet of the one with eight qualities is as useless as a sense organ without the power of perception.
ai.modern: எட்டு குணங்களை உடைய கடவுளின் திருவடிகளை வணங்காத தலைகள், அறியும் திறன் இல்லாத ஐம்பொறிகளைப் போல எந்தப் பயனும் இல்லாதவை ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares a head that refuses to bow to the divine to a defective sense organ. Just as an eye that cannot see or an ear that cannot hear lacks its defining quality, a head loses its true purpose if it does not show reverence. The phrase eṇkuṇattāṉ refers to the one possessing eight infinite qualities, representing the supreme being. The word kōḷ means the capacity to grasp or perceive, which is the essential function of any sense organ.
